Source: On arrival to the emergency department, the patient is not responding to verbal stimuli and only withdraws his left upper extremity and lower extremity to pain.
His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 170/100 mmHg, pulse is 95/min, and respirations are 16/min.
The patient has a seizure and subsequently demonstrates agonal breathing.
A 77-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a complaint of sudden onset weakness in his right upper extremity.
His past medical history is notable for hypertension and atrial fibrillation treated with metoprolol, apixaban, and lisinopril.
At home, the patient thought he was simply dehydrated, but he rapidly began to have trouble speaking.
A fingerstick blood glucose is 122 mg/dL.
He no longer responds to painful stimuli.
When his wife noted this she brought him into the hospital.
